correctness.rationale: For the printed discrete update T=(rho1 H tanh P, rho2 H(1-tanh P), alpha0 G+alpha H+(1-alpha)P), direct differentiation at zero gives DT(0)=[[0,0,0],[rho2,0,0],[alpha,1-alpha,alpha0]], hence multipliers 0,0,alpha0 strictly inside the unit disk for 0<alpha0<1. T is C1, so the origin is locally attracting. Independently at (rho1,rho2,alpha,alpha0)=(2,1,1/2,1/2), for strictly positive V=3H+P+G<1/16, tanh P<P<1/16 gives Hprime<=H/8, Pprime<=H, Gprime=(G+H+P)/2; therefore Vprime<=15H/8+P/2+G/2<=(3/4)V. The positive cone is invariant (tanh P in (0,1), alpha0>0), so this open positive set has V_n<=(3/4)^n V_0 and all coordinates tend to zero, contradicting Theorem 1’s universal strictly positive permanence liminf. For shared H0,P0 the G difference is alpha0^n deltaG0, because the first two equations contain no G.
residual_risks: Discrete T and difference field T-I must not be conflated; only T has multipliers 0,0,alpha0.
Contraction is shown for V<1/16 at one admissible tuple, not as a global statement for every positive initial point.
Six finite numerical orbits are corroboration only; the uniform-in-n conclusion follows from positivity and one-step induction.

evidence: The usual discrete hyperbolic fixed-point theorem implies local asymptotic stability once multipliers of this precise update are computed, but general theory alone does not identify or evaluate the printed PTM permanence theorem.

The 2016 refuge-effect model is a distinct two-dimensional recurrence with a constant refuge and no PTM environmental coordinate; the inspected abstract studies its persistence, not a correction of the tanh PTM map.

The 2024 article studies an arctan two-dimensional host–parasitoid activation model and compares the tanh model; it does not prove a stronger all-positive-initial-data extinction theorem for the printed three-dimensional map.
broader_coverage.reasoning: A genuinely dominating prior statement would invalidate permanence for the same printed recurrence and source parameter strip, or give a general theorem with hypotheses explicitly satisfied by that recurrence. The inspected works do not supply such a statement. The standard linearization theorem is a proof technique, not itself the model-specific priority claim.

value.rationale: Permanence is a substantive invariant for ecological/discrete population models: the original paper asserts a common positive asymptotic lower bound on every positive solution. This result invalidates that quantified conclusion inside the paper’s own parameter domain, with an open invariant positive basin and exact geometric convergence rather than an isolated orbit or superficial sign check. The passive third-coordinate identity also shows why varying PTM coefficients cannot rescue persistence of the first two populations in the printed model. Its significance is a precise correction to a central published theorem, not a claim of a globally classified basin or a new general local-stability theorem.
residual_risks: This is a targeted theorem correction using elementary dynamics, not a classification of all attractors or a new general theory.
Biological interpretation remains limited to the paper’s printed recurrence; no empirical disease inference is made.

final_claim: For the exact printed Salih--Al-Saidi Model (9) and rho1,rho2>0, 0<=alpha<=1, 0<alpha0<1, the discrete origin is locally asymptotically stable with multipliers (0,0,alpha0). In particular, admissible (rho1,rho2,alpha,alpha0)=(2,1,1/2,1/2) admits a strictly positive invariant open set 3H+P+G<1/16 whose solutions converge geometrically to (0,0,0), contradicting the published Theorem 1 claim of a common positive liminf under rho1>1, 0<rho2<=rho1, 0<alpha0<1. The H,P subsystem is independent of G and differences in G for equal H,P decay by alpha0^n. The correction is for the printed map only, not an altered PTM-feedback model or a full basin classification.
limitations: Only the printed 3D discrete update Model (9) is assessed; not the ODE model or alternative feedback rules.
The exact contraction is local at one admissible parameter tuple, and is sufficient to refute universal positive permanence.
